model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net_debt = 0

equity_bridge.item: CET1 released by announced divestitures (Transportation/Vendor Finance, 138 US branches, 50% Moneris)
equity_bridge.note: Q3-26 report Corporate Events: ~+50bp CET1 on closing x pro forma RWA ~443B = ~C$2.2B. Credited because FY0 earnings are already cut ~3% for the businesses sold; the capital is held above the 13.0% run-rate and is distributable (new 25M-share NCIB).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (book value per share FY2020 77.40 -> FY2025 111.57)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-year rates are distorted, not divergent fundamentals: FY2022 revenue (33,710) and EPS (19.99) include large fair-value gains on the Bank of the West purchase-price hedges, so every 3yr CAGR ending FY2025 runs from an inflated base (EPS 3yr -17%, NI 3yr -13.6% vs BVPS 3yr +5.3%). 5-year rates (FY2020 COVID-provision base) agree within 30%: equity 7.6%, revenue 7.6%, EPS 8.7%. The 5yr revenue CAGR also includes the Feb-2023 Bank of the West acquisition (inorganic), so the forward base path is set well below it (5.5% -> 3%).
historical_growth.notes: fcf_*_cagr fields carry REPORTED NET INCOME CAGRs (FY2022 13,537 / FY2020 5,097 -> FY2025 8,725): bank OCF/FCF swings with trading assets, deposits and securities and is not an owner cash flow. Adjusted NI FY2024 7,449 -> FY2025 9,248 (+24%); TTM adjusted 10,657.

scenario_narratives.base: BMO executes the March-2026 Investor Day plan: 4-6% revenue growth led by Capital Markets and Wealth (AUM C$604B, +30% YoY) plus steady commercial loan growth in both countries, 2%+ operating leverage taking adjusted efficiency to ~53%, credit near through-cycle (PCL ~0.43-0.45%). Lower-return pieces (Transportation/Vendor Finance, 138 U.S. branches, Moneris) are sold and the capital recycled into buybacks. Adjusted ROE reaches ~15% and ROTCE ~18.5-19% by FY2028, then plateaus; CET1 is run at ~13%.
scenario_narratives.bull: U.S. Banking finally closes the ROE gap to Canadian P&C after the portfolio clean-up, Capital Markets and Wealth sustain double-digit fee growth, and Canadian rate cuts reignite mortgage and commercial lending. Efficiency reaches ~51-52%, ROTCE ~20-21%, and BMO earns a premium among the Big Six.
scenario_narratives.bear: USMCA renegotiation fails, broad U.S. tariffs return and Canada enters recession in 2027-28: unemployment rises past 8%, unsecured consumer and commercial losses push PCL to ~0.8% of loans, Canadian housing softens on mortgage renewals at higher rates, and U.S. Banking returns stay at 7-8%. No solvency or funding case (CET1 13%, TLAC 29%, LCR 125%), but earnings power resets lower and the market prices BMO like a sub-par Big Six bank.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what common shareholders can take out: adjusted net income to common less the earnings that must be retained to hold CET1 at ~13% as the balance sheet grows, discounted at the CAD cost of equity. Deposits and wholesale funding are operating funding, so there is no net-debt deduction; preferred/AT1 distributions and NCI are removed inside the flow. Flows and the bridge are in CAD; the per-share result is converted to USD for comparison with the NYSE quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: PCL is ~7.7% of revenue at 0.43% of loans; a 0.8% year (bear) takes ~C$2.6B pre-tax out of one year's earnings.
Fee-cycle peak: Capital Markets and Wealth are posting 15-20%+ revenue growth on strong markets; a reversal hits the year-1 growth and margin directly.

Adjusted vs reported: the model uses adjusted earnings; BMO has booked recurring 'one-off' charges (Bank of the West integration, branch sale, C$1.0B goodwill charge on Transportation Finance). If such charges recur, adjusted overstates owner earnings.
Divestiture pro forma: the ~2% revenue / ~3% NI removed and the +50bp CET1 credited are management's estimates; final amounts depend on closing adjustments and FX.
FX: the CAD->USD conversion at 0.7019 moves the USD value one-for-one; roughly a third of earnings are USD-denominated, which partly hedges the translation.
Terminal value carries most of the value; the 14x FCFE cap and 3% CAD nominal terminal growth drive it.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE BMO, USD); TSX BMO.TO and CADUSD=X fetched for the parity check; 52-week range 119.84-187.22 USD
data_sources.financials: BMO Q3-2026 Report to Shareholders (Aug 25, 2026; Tables 1-2: reported and adjusted results, share data, CET1, RWA; Corporate Events: divestitures and pro forma impact; balance sheet: preferred and other equity 7,706, goodwill 16,086, intangibles 5,158); FY2025 Annual Report (adjusted results table, medium-term objectives, share-based payments); BMO_Metrics.csv / BMO.duckdb kpis for history (NII, non-interest revenue, BVPS, CET1, efficiency, ROE).
data_sources.qualitative: BMO_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): March-2026 Investor Day targets (adjusted ROE 15% by end-FY2027, ROTCE 18%+, EPS growth 7-10%, operating leverage 2%+, payout 40-50%), USMCA/credit risk framing.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report share-based payments line (54M FY25, 37M FY24; BMO_Annual_FY2025.txt:12312). Most BMO incentive pay is cash-settled share units already expensed in non-interest expense; the equity-settled charge is ~C$50M/yr and is charged in the flows via sbc_pct_path.
inputs.fx_note: CAD->USD 0.7019 (Yahoo CADUSD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-03T21:00Z). Parity check: TSX BMO.TO C$236.25 x 0.7019 = US$165.82 vs NYSE BMO US$165.70 (0.07% gap). One NYSE share = one TSX common share. Flows, CoE and equity bridge are CAD; unsuffixed intrinsic values are converted to USD for comparison with the NYSE price.
inputs.fy0: TTM to 2026-07-31 (adjusted basis, pro forma for announced divestitures)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, NYSE BMO)
inputs.share_count_basis: 697.1M common shares outstanding at 2026-07-31 (Q3-26 report Table 1) + 2.3M dilutive (Q3 average diluted 701.7M vs basic 699.4M) = 699.4M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is charged in the flows and buybacks (3.8M shares in Q3 at C$239; new NCIB for up to 25M shares pending OSFI/TSX approval) are a use of the FCFE already being valued. buyback_cash is the Q3-26 quarter's 3.8M x C$239.37 ~ C$0.9B.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY in CAD, not a WACC: the flow is post-interest, post-preferred FCFE. Canada 10y ~3.4% + beta ~1.1 x 5.75% ERP = ~9.7%; base 9.75%. Bull 9.5%; bear 10.25% (only +50bp because the bear credit path already carries most of the downside -- charge risk once). Same cost-of-equity framework as NAB.AX (9.7%) and USB (10.0%), adjusted for the lower Canadian risk-free rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: n/a -- bank; premises/lease cost is inside non-interest expense, no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Preferred dividends + LRCN/AT1 distributions + NCI income (TTM C$476M adjusted: FY25 436+NCI less YTD25, plus YTD26 301+5) are removed INSIDE the flow as a pre-tax equivalent (~C$630M at 24.4%), so the after-tax flow is net income to COMMON. Preferred shares and other equity instruments (C$7,706M at 2026-07-31) are therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge (USB precedent; doing both charges them twice).
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (house precedent USB, TFC, HBAN, NTRS, STT, NAB.AX; SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book -- FCFE-at-CoE with retention = growth x regulatory capital is the equivalent flow form and keeps BMO comparable with the other banks in this folder). No prior BMO valuation and no memory entry: first build. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = net interest income + non-interest revenue; 'ebitda' = adjusted pre-tax income + SBC - pre-tax-equivalent(pref/AT1 distributions + NCI); D&A 0; 'capex' = capital retention needed to keep CET1 at 13.0% as RWA grows with revenue = CET1/revenue 1.518 x g/(1+g); wc 0; net_debt 0 (deposits, senior notes and the C$7.5B subordinated debt are operating funding/regulatory capital, not acquisition debt). TTM BUILD (adjusted, C$M; Q4-FY25 = FY25 adjusted less YTD-Q3-FY25 adjusted): revenue 9,341 + 29,373 = 38,714; PCL 755 + 2,207 = 2,962 (7.7% of revenue, 0.43% of loans -- near through-cycle); NIE 5,294 + 16,371 = 21,665 (efficiency 56.0%); pre-tax 3,292 + 10,795 = 14,087; tax 3,430 (24.4%); NI 10,657; NI to common 10,181. ADJUSTED, NOT REPORTED: TTM reported NI 9,164 carries the Q3-26 C$962M after-tax goodwill charge on the Transportation/Vendor Finance sale, branch-sale costs, Burgundy contingent-consideration remeasurement (C$86M) and acquired-intangible amortisation (~C$280M/yr after tax; non-cash, and goodwill/intangibles are already deducted from CET1). PRO FORMA: the Transportation/Vendor Finance sale (Stonepeak), the 138-branch sale (closed 2026-09-04) and the 50% Moneris sale contributed ~2% of adjusted revenue and ~3% of adjusted NI in Q3-26 (Q3-26 report, Corporate Events), so FY0 revenue = 38,714 x 0.98 = 37,940 and pre-tax x 0.97 = 13,664; ebitda = 13,664 + 50 - 630 = 13,084 = 34.5% of revenue; NI to common pro forma ~9,876. The capital these sales release (+~50bp CET1 on closing, incl. the ~C$600M after-tax Moneris gain) is credited in the equity bridge. CET1: 13.0% x RWA 454,757 = C$59.1B at 2026-07-31; pro forma RWA ~443B after the sold loan books, CET1 at 13.0% = C$57.6B = 1.518x pro forma revenue. last_fcf 7,134 = pro forma NI to common 9,876 less retention at 5% growth (2,742) -- an FCFE proxy, since bank OCF (C$+26.7B in Q3-26 alone, -C$4.2B in Q3-25) is balance-sheet noise, not owner cash.
inputs.price_note: Regular-session close (Friday 2026-10-02), not an after-hours print.

bear.margin_rationale: Failed USMCA renegotiation tips Canada into recession in year 2: PCL roughly doubles to ~0.8% of loans (~14% of revenue, the FY2020 level was 0.9%), revenue flat as loan growth stalls and NIM compresses with BoC cuts; margin recovers only to 33.5% (below today's 34.5%) because the efficiency programme stalls and U.S. Banking stays sub-par.

base.margin_rationale: Delivers the medium-term framework (adjusted operating leverage 2%+, ROE 15% by end-FY2027, ROTCE 18%+): adjusted efficiency 56.0% TTM falls ~1pp/yr for three years to ~53%, PCL held ~0.43-0.45% of loans (~7.5% of revenue). Margin 34.5% FY0 pro forma -> 36.8% by year 4, then flat. Implied year-3 adjusted ROTCE ~18.5-19% on ~C$62-65B TCE -- at the target, not above it.
base.capex_rationale: Retention = CET1/revenue 1.518 x g/(1+g): keeps CET1 at 13.0% as RWA grows with revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): the USMCA renegotiation is a near-term macro binary that BMO's own outlook names as the path to a Canadian recession, Canadian unemployment is already rising, and bank earnings are levered to credit. Base 50%: Q3-26 adjusted results (ROE 14.0%, record pre-provision earnings in every segment) are tracking the plan. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it requires both a U.S. Banking turnaround and sustained capital-markets strength at what is already a strong point in the fee cycle.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
